title: Open-immersion and etale extension by zero have the same adjunction
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open immersion of schemes [def-weil-open-immersion], which is etale [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and let $\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ be the category of sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $T=U,X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $j_!$ be the extension by zero of [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], the sheafification of the presheaf $j_{p!}F$, with the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] (unit $\eta_j$, counit $\varepsilon_j$), where $j^{-1}$ is the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Let $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ be the extension $v_!$ of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension] for $v=j$, the sheafification of $V\mapsto\bigoplus_{s\in\Hom_X(V,U)}F(V,s)$, with the adjunction $j^{\mathrm{et}}_!\dashv j^{-1}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] (unit $\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_j$, counit $\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_j$), the adjunction used in [def-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-map]. For $F\in\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $V\in X_{\Et}$ let $\iota_{F,V}:(j_{p!}F)(V)\to\bigoplus_{s\in\Hom_X(V,U)}F(V,s)$ be the inclusion of $F(V\xrightarrow{\varphi}U)$ as the unique summand when $V$ factors through $U$ by $\varphi$, and the zero map of zero modules otherwise, and let $\kappa_F:j_!F\to j^{\mathrm{et}}_!F$ be the sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] of $\iota_F$. Then $\kappa$ is a natural isomorphism $j_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$ of functors $\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)\to\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and it identifies the two adjunctions: for $F\in\Mod(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$, $G\in\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $\alpha:F\to j^{-1}G$, the transpose of $\alpha$ under the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is the transpose of $\alpha$ under the adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-restriction-injectives] composed with $\kappa_F$. Equivalently $\eta^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,F}=j^{-1}(\kappa_F)\circ\eta_{j,F}$ and $\varepsilon_{j,G}=\varepsilon^{\mathrm{et}}_{j,G}\circ\kappa_{j^{-1}G}$.
